whose: OpenAI Codex, under L66, from the sealed corpus

sentences.1: Natural selection acts wherever there are things that vary, that pass on what they are, and that leave different numbers of descendants because of it.
sentences.3: A group whose members help one another at a cost to themselves leaves more descendant groups than a group of members who do not, because the helping group outlasts, outgrows or outfights its rivals.
sentences.4: Within any one group, a member who helps does worse than a member who does not, because the helper pays the cost and every member shares the benefit.
sentences.5: So selection within groups works against helping, and selection between groups works for it.
sentences.6: Which wins depends on how much the groups differ from one another and how much the members differ within them.
sentences.7: When groups differ greatly, because helpers cluster together and stay together, selection between groups is the stronger, and helping spreads.
sentences.8: This is not a way of speaking; it is a cause: the group structure produces the spread of helping, and remove the structure and the spread stops.
sentences.9: Accounting that credits the spread to the individual's relatives is arithmetic done afterwards, and it does not change what produced the outcome.
sentences.10: Where cooperation has spread, as in the social insects, the cell, and the human tribe, groups were the things selection was acting on.

leftover: Sentence 1: “Natural selection acts wherever there are things that vary, that pass on what they are, and that leave different numbers of descendants because of it.” — The selection criterion includes differing descendant numbers caused by variation/inheritance. Quantities and combined causal contributors cannot be removed without altering the condition; retain it in full here.
Sentence 2: “Groups can be such things.” — Possibility can, not an actual instantiated group satisfying the criteria.

Sentence 3: “A group whose members help one another at a cost to themselves leaves more descendant groups than a group of members who do not, because the helping group outlasts, outgrows or outfights its rivals.” — The descendant-count comparison is conditional on costly helping. Outlasting/outgrowing/outfighting are alternatives; no one is selected as an actual cause, and no amount-free reproductive inequality is fabricated.
Sentence 4: “because the helper pays the cost and every member shares the benefit” — Joint explanatory contributors and uncomputed cost/benefit quantities. No one reason is substituted for both.
Sentence 5: “So” — Support runs through the quantified comparisons above; no executable sufficient bridge is supplied.

Sentence 6: “Which wins depends on how much the groups differ from one another and how much the members differ within them.” — Outcome depends on how much variation, not merely whether a difference is present. Magnitude-dependent dependence stays in the bin.

Sentence 7: “When groups differ greatly, because helpers cluster together and stay together, selection between groups is the stronger, and helping spreads.” — The conditional contains greatly and stronger. Clustering/staying are nested in that explanation, not unconditionally asserted events; dropping the degree conditions would alter the spread claim.

Sentence 8: “not a way of speaking; stops” — The source denial of being a way of speaking is retained without adding merely. Stopping time/cessation are not modelled: j asks whether spread remains true after removal. No production law is added from the BECAUSE claim alone.
Sentence 9: “credits the spread to the individual's relatives; afterwards” — Attribution and exact time not checked; arithmetic remains an opaque description, not executed mathematics.
